solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tool for piercing tag of leather kept in closet?

indicators.note: a tag is the tail end of something, so only the final letter of the next word is wanted
something kept in a place sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: bog is slang for a toilet, a water closet
the last letter of leather

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what tool might pierce a leather tag hidden away in a cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Closet is the toilet sense, as in water closet; bog is the British slang word for it. A brog is a Scots word for an awl.
explanation.definitionFit: A brog is an awl or bradawl, a small pointed tool used for boring holes in leather or wood.

clue.text: False god engaging large number in flat

indicators.note: to engage something is to take it in and hold it, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: Baal was the Canaanite deity condemned in the Bible as a false god
n stands for an indefinitely large number in maths

explanation.surface: An idol worshipped by huge crowds turns out to be dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat in the sense of lacking interest or sparkle is a synonym of trite and unoriginal.

clue.text: Miscellaneous collection on a main ground

indicators.note: something ground is crushed and broken up, so these letters are reduced and reformed

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A jumble of odds and ends is gathered up on a main field.
explanation.definitionFit: Omniana is a Latin-derived word for notes or writings about all sorts of things, a miscellany.

clue.text: Ceremonial seat seen with historic rod and Crown of India?

indicators.note: the crown is the top of something, and in a down entry the top is the first letter

blocks.note: gad is an old word for a rod or goad
the first letter of India

explanation.surface: A throne is pictured alongside an ancient sceptre and the crown jewels of the Raj.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Crown of India is not regalia but the top letter of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadi is the cushioned throne of an Indian ruler, so it is a seat of state used on ceremonial occasions.

clue.text: Sign of damage in disease for worms

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: the immune deficiency syndrome
a scar is the mark left by an injury

explanation.surface: Tissue scarred by illness is blamed on parasitic worms.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascarids are parasitic roundworms of the genus Ascaris, found in the intestines of humans and animals.

clue.text: A member's cape that's worn outside?

definitions.text: A member's cape that's worn outside?

indicators.note: a garment worn outside goes round whatever is beneath it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for member, as in MP
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a club member's cape is the kind worn over everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the abbreviation for that is goes round the cape's letter. Read as a whole, it describes a vestment a member of the clergy wears.
explanation.definitionFit: An amice is a linen cloth a priest wears round the neck and shoulders, outside the alb, like a small cape.

clue.text: Series on US prisons getting a lot of stars

blocks.note: ser. is the abbreviation for series
pen is American slang for a penitentiary; on places it after the first piece in a down entry

explanation.surface: A television series about American jails earns a string of star ratings.
explanation.definitionFit: Serpens, the Serpent, is a constellation, so it is a large group of stars.

clue.text: Wife sharing top room close to home in two stages

indicators.note: one who shares a room is lodged inside it, so a single letter goes within the room
the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

blocks.note: the attic is the room at the top of a house
W is the abbreviation for wife
the last letter of home

explanation.surface: A wife moves into the loft near the house, a project done in two phases.
explanation.walkthrough: At twice is an old Spenserian phrase found in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: At twice is an archaic adverbial phrase meaning on two occasions, so done in two goes or stages.

clue.text: Having several branches, Standard banks advance millions

indicators.note: banks line the sides of a river, so one word flanks the letters that follow it

blocks.note: a rate is a standard or level, as in first-rate
a. is a dictionary abbreviation for advance, as in a credit advance
M is the abbreviation for millions

explanation.surface: A bank with many branches, Standard Chartered perhaps, lends out millions.
explanation.walkthrough: Standard and banks both suggest a bank like Standard Chartered; here the first is a word meaning level and the second is the containment instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramate is a botanical term for branched, from Latin ramus, a branch.

clue.text: One saying no residents represented

indicators.note: to represent something is to present it again in another form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lone objector speaks up while the local people are represented at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissenter is someone who disagrees or refuses to accept an opinion, so a person voting no.

clue.text: Some turned up in crack military unit for provincial governors

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning something up means reading it from the bottom upwards
one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: some of a thing is part of it
the Special Air Service, the British army's elite regiment

explanation.surface: A few commandos appear among the troops guarding regional rulers.
explanation.definitionFit: Satraps were the governors of provinces in the ancient Persian empire.

clue.text: Resources meant to be marshalled in a case of major back strain?

indicators.note: the case of something is its outside, so only the outer letters of the word are taken
going back means those letters are read in the opposite direction
troops marshalled are put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the outer letters of major
taken as written
a strain is a melody, and an aria is a solo song

explanation.surface: Military resources are mustered for a major who has hurt his back.
explanation.walkthrough: Marshalled and major suggest the army, but the major only supplies its two outside letters, read backwards. The anagram goes in after them, before the song.
explanation.definitionFit: Armamentaria is the plural of armamentarium, the full stock of equipment and resources available for a task.

clue.text: Saving skin Indians slaughtered bear?

indicators.note: saving here means except, so the outer layer of the word is left out
something slaughtered is butchered and cut up, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Hunters kill a bear but are careful to keep its hide intact.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as doubtful: the Nandi bear is a creature of East African folklore whose existence is unproven.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nandi bear is a legendary animal said to live in Kenya, named after the Nandi people.

clue.text: Not more than one rugby official starts to satisfy Twickenham

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters, so only those are taken

blocks.note: a means one
the TMO is the television match official who reviews rugby replays
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: One video referee aims to please the crowd at Twickenham, England's rugby stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Twickenham is the home ground of English rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: At most is the idiom for an upper limit, meaning no more than a given amount.

clue.text: Expert on tuck initiated twisting

indicators.note: something twisting is bent out of its shape, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A new recruit learns a fancy dive with a twisting tuck.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuck looks like a gymnastics or diving position; here it is British school slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: A dietitian is a professional adviser on nutrition, and tuck is informal British slang for food, especially sweets.

clue.text: Break said to be about a week for conferences

indicators.note: said tells us to use a word that sounds like the one meant, not its spelling
about means around, so the outer word goes round the inner

blocks.note: a pause is a short break
a, plus W, the abbreviation for week

explanation.surface: A short break turns out to last about a week, all spent in meetings.
explanation.definitionFit: Pawaw is a Chambers variant spelling of powwow, a meeting or conference.

clue.text: End of razor-like spike reversed for a climber

indicators.note: reversed means the word is read from its last letter to its first
the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: a nail is a metal spike
the last letter of razor-like

explanation.surface: A sharp spike is turned round to protect a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: Climber suggests a mountaineer but means a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Liane is a variant of liana, a woody climbing plant of tropical forests.

clue.text: Country leaders wanted in desert region

indicators.note: wanted here means lacking, so each word loses its leading letter

blocks.note: to merit is to deserve, the verb sense of desert as in just deserts
a region is an area

explanation.surface: Wanted posters for leaders hang in a desert part of a country.
explanation.walkthrough: Desert is a verb here, meaning deserve, not a sandy region; both words then lose their first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a nation in the Horn of Africa on the Red Sea coast.

clue.text: Forward close in scrum initially clinging to leg

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word before it
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the first letter of scrum
the close is the end
leg and on are the same side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A rugby forward stays close in the scrum, grabbing an opponent's leg.
explanation.walkthrough: Forward is the definition as a verb, though the rugby surface makes it a player. The leg side and the on side are the same half of a cricket field.
explanation.definitionFit: To send on is to forward a letter or parcel to a new address.

clue.text: Series of mouldings on French home

blocks.note: sur is French for on
a base is a home, as in home base

explanation.surface: A row of decorative mouldings is fitted in a house in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A surbase is the cornice or moulding run above a skirting board or along the top of a pedestal.

clue.text: Tiles built up a third-class cold painting well

indicators.note: in a down entry, building upwards means the letters are read from the bottom

blocks.note: taken as written
surplus: it would give a second C the answer lacks, so it reads as padding or a setter's slip
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
painting is a form of art
so and well both open a remark, as in so, what next

explanation.surface: Tiles are used to build up a cheap painted well.
explanation.walkthrough: Third-class looks like a second source of C, but the answer has only one, so one of it and cold is surplus; the blog suspected a slip. Some read third-class as the third letter of class.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostraca are potsherds or tile fragments used in antiquity as writing surfaces, as for votes of ostracism.

clue.text: Note found in Asian sea giving muster of a force

indicators.note: something found in a place lies inside it

blocks.note: the Aral Sea in Central Asia
ray is a variant of re, the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A naval force is mustered on an Asian sea after a signal is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrayal is an old word for the act of arraying, the drawing up of troops for review.

clue.text: Style shown by Jerry, supplier of chips

blocks.note: a jerry is British slang for a chamber pot, a po
Intel makes computer processor chips

explanation.surface: Jerry flaunts his style, as you would expect of someone who sells chips.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerry looks like a name, but a jerry is a chamber pot, also called a po. Chips are silicon, not fried potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointel is an old word for a stylus or pencil, and a style is a pointed writing instrument.

clue.text: One German car in competition with another after final 25 per cent discount

indicators.note: a discount of the final quarter means the last letter of four is knocked off

blocks.note: a bee is a contest, as in a spelling bee
Merc is short for Mercedes, another German car

explanation.surface: A German car races another, which has been sold off at a quarter below price.
explanation.walkthrough: A bee is a gathering for a competition, as in a spelling bee. The Merc loses one of its four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Beemer is slang for a BMW, a German make of car.

clue.text: Pressure dropping, plug back in sinks again

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it fall away, so one letter is lost
back means the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure
a stopper is a plug

explanation.surface: With the water pressure gone, someone puts the plug back in the kitchen sinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Sinks and plug suggest plumbing, and repots suggests gardening, but here to pot is to sink a ball in snooker.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker or pool, to pot a ball is to sink it in a pocket, so repots means sinks again.

clue.text: Test perhaps around half-term is a clincher

indicators.note: around means the outer word is wrapped round the inner piece
half of a word means only its first two of four letters are kept

blocks.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire, England
the first half of term

explanation.surface: A school test held around half-term proves decisive.
explanation.walkthrough: Test is a proper noun here, the River Test, famous for trout fishing; the perhaps marks it as one example of a river. The half goes in after RIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A clincher is a person or tool that clinches, bending over the ends of nails or rivets, which is a riveter's job.

clue.text: Bound to restrict Queen being heard

indicators.note: to restrict something is to hem it in, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: bound means tied up
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A queen is tied up and held captive, her cries being heard.
explanation.walkthrough: Being heard is a court case being heard by a judge, not sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A case that is being tried is being heard before a court, so tried matches the legal sense of heard.

clue.text: Metal armbands in discussions overheard

indicators.note: something overheard is only caught by ear, so the spelling is not the one that sounds

blocks.note: talks are discussions

explanation.surface: Talk of metal arm-rings is caught by an eavesdropper.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works in a non-rhotic British accent, where the R is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is a twisted metal neck ring or armlet worn by ancient Celts.

clue.text: Seaweed from delta followed by two universities

blocks.note: Delta is D in the NATO phonetic alphabet
U for university, plus the LSE, the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: Seaweed is found on a river delta, followed by a pair of college researchers.
explanation.walkthrough: The LSE is the London School of Economics, part of the University of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Dulse is an edible red seaweed found on Atlantic coasts.

clue.text: My Moroccan house mostly used for group to which old men belong

definitions.text: group to which old men belong

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is cut

blocks.note: the can mean my, as in the wife for my wife
a riad is a traditional Moroccan house with a courtyard

explanation.surface: Someone's Moroccan house is let to a club for elderly gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: Old men here are not elderly people: in Australian slang an old man is a full-grown male kangaroo. My gives the colloquial the, as in the missus.
explanation.definitionFit: Theria is the subclass of mammals including marsupials such as kangaroos, so male kangaroos belong to it.

clue.text: Run out of plant pots

indicators.note: out of here means taken away from, so a letter leaves the word

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a plant is a factory, or works

explanation.surface: Someone has run out of plant pots for the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant pots reads as one gardening item; plant is a factory and pots is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Woks are Chinese cooking pans, a kind of pot used for stir-frying.

clue.text: Prosperous Middle East state ignoring Foreign Office flyer

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: fair means favourable or promising, as in fair prospects
Oman is a state on the Arabian peninsula
the FO, Britain's Foreign Office

explanation.surface: A wealthy Gulf state snubs the British Foreign Office and sends a pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters are removed one from each word: the F from the front of the first and the O from the front of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: An airman is a pilot or member of an air force, someone who flies.

clue.text: Get round West End of London on wheels

indicators.note: on a map west is the left, so the west end of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a rota is a round of duties taken in turn
the first letter of London

explanation.surface: Someone tours the West End of London on a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: West End looks like the theatre district, but it means the left-hand end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotal is a rare adjective meaning relating to wheels, from Latin rota, a wheel.

clue.text: They'd take deposits from Peter and Dotty

blocks.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
dotty and crackers both mean mad

explanation.surface: Two people, Peter and Dotty, collect deposits like bank tellers.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter and Dotty look like first names; a peter is underworld slang for a safe, and dotty means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Safecrackers break open safes and take what has been deposited in them, a wry view of deposit-taking.

clue.text: Black leaving mountain-top paths? Lights needed

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter is taken off

blocks.note: B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
ben is a Scottish word for a mountain peak, as in Ben Nevis
trails are paths

explanation.surface: Hikers need torches once darkness falls on the mountain trails.
explanation.walkthrough: Lights look like lamps for the walk, but lights are the lungs of a slaughtered animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lights are animal lungs used as offal, so they are among the entrails, the internal organs.

clue.text: Mclaren's black and bluish grey Tesla rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: slate is a bluish-grey colour
T is the SI symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: A McLaren racing car in black and slate grey beats a Tesla that was turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: McLaren and Tesla suggest cars, but McLaren is the Scots dictionary, and the tesla is a unit of physics. Black is the sloe, the blackthorn fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Slae is the Scots spelling of sloe, the small black fruit of the blackthorn, listed in Mclaren's Scots dictionary.
